title: A housebound engineer and his wife finished the Brooklyn Bridge
body: John Roebling designed the Brooklyn Bridge but died of tetanus in 1869 after an accident at the site. His son Washington took over, then was disabled by decompression sickness, or caisson disease, from working in the pressurised chambers used to dig the foundations. His wife, Emily Warren Roebling, studied engineering and relayed his instructions to the site for more than ten years. When the bridge opened in 1883, she was the first to ride across.
